\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{تربیت} (tarbiyat)}{تربیت (tarbiyat)}]{\ur{تربیت} (tarbiyat) — upbringing; training}

\label{lesson:UR-C384-tarbiyat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to rake in, then the Urdu for to fail an exam.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{تربیت}}
\textbf{\ur{تربیت}} — \emph{tarbiyat} — \textquotedblleft{}upbringing; training\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{تربیت} \ur{اچھی} \ur{ہوئی} \ur{تو} \ur{بچے} \ur{اچھے} \ur{بنیں} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar tarbiyat achchhī huī to bachche achchhe baneṅ ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If they are brought up well, children will turn out well.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{تربیت}} (\emph{tarbiyat}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{tarbiya}, \textquotedblleft{}bringing up, rearing\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tarbiyat}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tarbiyat}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar tarbiyat achchhī huī to bachche achchhe baneṅ ge.} — If they are brought up well, children will turn out well.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to rake in, then the Urdu for to fail an exam, then say \emph{tarbiyat} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{تربیت} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Upbringing; training\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{فراخ} \ur{دل} (farākh-dil)}{فراخ دل (farākh-dil)}]{\ur{فراخ} \ur{دل} (farākh-dil) — generous; big-hearted}

\label{lesson:UR-C384-farakh-dil}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to fail an exam, then the Urdu for upbringing.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{فراخ} \ur{دل}}
\textbf{\ur{فراخ} \ur{دل}} — \emph{farākh-dil} — \textquotedblleft{}generous; big-hearted\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{وہ} \ur{فراخ} \ur{دل} \ur{ہوتا} \ur{تو} \ur{مدد} \ur{کرتا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar voh farākh-dil hotā to madad kartā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If he were generous, he would help.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{فراخ} \ur{دل}} (\emph{farākh-dil}) is built from Persian \emph{farākh}, \textquotedblleft{}wide\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\ur{دل}}, \textquotedblleft{}heart\textquotedblright{}, usually traced to Persian \emph{dil}: a wide heart.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{آداب} (ādāb)}{آداب (ādāb)}]{\ur{آداب} (ādāb) — manners; respects}

\label{lesson:UR-C384-adab}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for upbringing, then the Urdu for generous.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{آداب}}
\textbf{\ur{آداب}} — \emph{ādāb} — \textquotedblleft{}manners; respects\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{آداب} \ur{سیکھیے،} \ur{ورنہ} \ur{لوگ} \ur{برا} \ur{کہیں} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ādāb sīkhiye, varnā log burā kaheṅ ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Learn some manners, or people will speak ill of you.
\end{quote}

Masculine, used in the plural.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{آداب}} (\emph{ādāb}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ādāb}, the plural of \emph{adab}, \textquotedblleft{}good manners\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{لاڈ} (lāḍ)}{لاڈ (lāḍ)}]{\ur{لاڈ} (lāḍ) — pampering; fond indulgence}

\label{lesson:UR-C384-lad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for generous, then the Urdu for manners.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{لاڈ}}
\textbf{\ur{لاڈ}} — \emph{lāḍ} — \textquotedblleft{}pampering; fond indulgence\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{آپ} \ur{نے} \ur{بہت} \ur{لاڈ} \ur{کیا} \ur{تو} \ur{بچہ} \ur{بگڑے} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar āp ne bahut lāḍ kiyā to bachchā bigṛe gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you pamper the child too much, he will be spoilt.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{لاڈ}} (\emph{lāḍ}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{lāṛ}, \textquotedblleft{}affection\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{*lāḍya}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 11013).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{رٹنا} (raṭnā)}{رٹنا (raṭnā)}]{\ur{رٹنا} (raṭnā) — to learn by rote; to cram}

\label{lesson:UR-C384-ratna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for manners, then the Urdu for pampering.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{رٹنا}}
\textbf{\ur{رٹنا}} — \emph{raṭnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to learn by rote; to cram\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{تم} \ur{صرف} \ur{رٹو} \ur{گے} \ur{تو} \ur{کچھ} \ur{نہیں} \ur{سمجھو} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar tum sirf raṭo ge to kuchh nahīṅ samjho ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you only learn by rote, you will understand nothing.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{سبق} \ur{رٹا}, \emph{us ne sabaq raṭā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{رٹنا}} (\emph{raṭnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{raṭnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to cry out, to repeat\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{ráṭati}, \textquotedblleft{}cries out\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 10590): saying a thing over and over.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\end{itemize}
